sources.author: Li, Wendong, et al.

sources.author: Follis, Kathryn, et al.
sources.title: Furin cleavage of the SARS coronavirus spike glycoprotein enhances cell–cell fusion but does not affect virion entry
sources.summary: 2006 Virology study inserting a furin cleavage site at the SARS-CoV S1–S2 junction—showing the technique was already known (chapter notes).

sources.author: Roberts, Anjeanette, et al.
sources.title: A Mouse-Adapted SARS-Coronavirus Causes Disease and Mortality in BALB/c Mice
sources.summary: 2007 PLOS Pathogens study creating a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV that causes disease and mortality in BALB/c mice via serial passage—lab evolution of pathogenicity.
sources.book_role: Baric-lineage work adapting SARS-CoV-1 in mice—step two of the research trajectory Chapter 12 traces.

sources.author: Baric, Ralph
sources.title: Synthetic Viral Genomics: Risks and Benefits for Science and Society
sources.summary: 2007 Baric paper on risks and benefits of synthetic viral genomics—early articulation of dual-use coronavirus reverse-genetics capabilities from a central U.S. practitioner.
sources.book_role: Primary statement from Baric on synthetic virus tech’s dual-use stakes inside the biodefense complex.

sources.author: Ren, Wuze, et al.
sources.title: Difference in Receptor Usage Between Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) Coronavirus and SARS-Like Coronavirus of Bat Origin
sources.summary: 2008 JVI Shi-associated paper on receptor-usage differences; chapter notes: chimeric spikes showed bat SARS-like CoVs could be modified to infect human cells. PubMed scrape failed.
sources.book_role: Documents WIV capability to retarget bat CoV spikes toward human cells.

sources.title: Anthrax scientist commits suicide as FBI closes in
sources.summary: AP/CBC report on Bruce Ivins’s suicide as FBI prepared to indict him in the 2001 anthrax-letter attacks—foundational trauma of the U.S. biodefense era.
sources.book_role: Historical anchor: domestic bioweapons lab insider threat that turbocharged post-anthrax biodefense spending.

sources.author: Becker, Michelle, et al.
sources.title: Synthetic recombinant bat SARS-like coronavirus is infectious in cultured cells and in mice
sources.summary: 2008 PNAS paper on a synthetic recombinant bat SARS-like coronavirus infectious in cells and mice—spike/backbone chimera work in the Baric orbit.
sources.book_role: Shows insertion of SARS spike into a synthetic backbone—bridging bat CoV genetics and mammalian infection (chapter notes).

sources.author: Hoffman, David
sources.title: The Dead Hand: The Untold Story of the Cold War Arms Race and Its Dangerous Legacy
sources.summary: Amazon product page for David Hoffman’s history of Cold War nuclear/biological arms racing and the Soviet ‘Dead Hand’ legacy. Page is a retail landing page, not book text.
sources.book_role: Background reading on Cold War biological-weapons history informing Chapter 2’s bioweapons frame.

sources.author: Taleb, Nassim
sources.title: The Black Swan: The Impact of the Highly Improbable
sources.summary: Nassim Taleb’s book on highly improbable, high-impact events. No URL in the bibliography; cited as conceptual background for pandemic fat-tail risk.
sources.book_role: Intellectual backdrop for treating the new coronavirus as a Black Swan–style systemic risk rather than a routine outbreak.

sources.title: Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) proteins of different bat species confer variable susceptibility to SARS-CoV entry
sources.summary: 2010 Archives of Virology study testing ACE2 from different bat species for variable SARS-CoV entry susceptibility—mapping which bat receptors allow infection.
sources.book_role: Shows WIV systematically probing bat ACE2 compatibility with SARS entry.

sources.author: Herfst, Sander, et al.
sources.title: Airborne Transmission of Influenza A/H5N1 Virus Between Ferrets
sources.summary: Landmark Science paper demonstrating airborne transmission of H5N1 influenza between ferrets—central exhibit in gain-of-function controversy.

sources.author: Fauci, Anthony S.
sources.title: Research on Highly Pathogenic H5N1 Influenza Virus: The Way Forward
sources.summary: Fauci’s 2012 mBio commentary defending a path forward for highly pathogenic H5N1 research amid gain-of-function controversy.

sources.author: Xu, Li
sources.title: Analysis of Six Patients With Unknown Viruses
sources.summary: English translation of Li Xu’s 2013 Kunming Medical University master’s thesis analyzing six Mojiang miners with severe pneumonia from unknown viruses—clinical detail on the 2012 outbreak.
sources.book_role: Primary clinical document of the Mojiang miner illnesses Chapter 11 centers on.

sources.author: Xing-Yi Ge, et al.
sources.title: Isolation and characterization of a bat SARS-like coronavirus that uses the ACE2 receptor
sources.summary: Landmark 2013 Nature paper isolating a bat SARS-like coronavirus that uses ACE2—foundational WIV work showing bat sarbecoviruses can bind the human receptor years before COVID.
sources.book_role: Establishes WIV’s pre-pandemic ACE2-using bat CoV research program that Mojiang sampling sits inside.

sources.author: Richards, Stephanie, et al.
sources.title: BSL-3 Laboratory Practices in the United States: Comparison of Select Agent and Non–Select Agent Facilities
sources.publication: Biosecurity and Bioterrorism: Biodefense Strategy, Practice, and Science
sources.summary: 2014 survey comparing BSL-3 practices at U.S. select-agent versus non–select-agent facilities—empirical look at biosafety variation inside the domestic biodefense lab network.
sources.book_role: Technical evidence that U.S. high-containment practice itself is uneven—context for exporting risky work abroad.

sources.author: Furmanski, Martin
sources.title: Threatened pandemics and laboratory escapes: Self-fulfilling prophecies
sources.summary: Bulletin essay warning that gain-of-function work on potential pandemic pathogens creates a self-fulfilling risk of laboratory escape, surveying historical lab-escape episodes and biosafety debates.
sources.book_role: Establishes that lab-escape pandemics were a serious, mainstream biosafety concern years before COVID—before such talk was branded conspiracy theory.

sources.title: Understanding the Risk of Bat Coronavirus Emergence
sources.summary: NIH RePORTER record for EcoHealth/Daszak project ‘Understanding the Risk of Bat Coronavirus Emergence’ (2R01AI110964)—the bat-CoV grant at the center of Wuhan collaboration funding fights.
sources.book_role: Primary grant record tying U.S. NIH money to the bat-coronavirus work floodgate debates reopen.

sources.summary: 2014 review of coronavirus reverse-genetic systems—infectious clones and replicons enabling engineered CoV recovery.

sources.author: Menachery, Vineet, et al.
sources.title: A SARS-like cluster of circulating bat coronaviruses shows potential for human emergence
sources.summary: 2015 Nature Medicine study (Menachery/Baric et al.) showing a SARS-like bat coronavirus cluster with potential for human emergence; later cited in COVID origin debates (with a 2020 editors’ note rejecting unverified engineering claims).
sources.book_role: Pre-pandemic chimeric/bat-CoV research paper that Chapter 5 uses to show human-emergence potential was already being demonstrated in the lab years earlier.

sources.author: Ge, X.Y., et al.
sources.title: Coexistence of multiple coronaviruses in several bat colonies in an abandoned mineshaft
sources.summary: 2016 Virologica Sinica paper documenting multiple coronaviruses coexisting in bat colonies in an abandoned mineshaft—the Mojiang site later tied to RaTG13/BtCoV/4991.
sources.book_role: Primary scientific record of WIV sampling in the Mojiang mineshaft before the pandemic.

sources.title: Coexistence of multiple coronaviruses in several bat colonies in an abandoned mineshaft

sources.book_role: Shows RaTG13 existed in public databases since 2016 under the 4991 name—key Mojiang breadcrumb.

sources.book_role: Supports the chapter’s point about China’s air-travel volume and how quickly an emerging pathogen could seed abroad.

sources.title: Identifying conspiracy theories
sources.summary: EU Commission/UNESCO guide listing traits of conspiracy theories and, under COVID-19, explicitly treating claims that the virus was artificially created in a laboratory as dangerous conspiracy theories—guidance that remains online.

sources.title: Personal journal

sources.book_role: Anchors Chapter 1 in the author’s own contemporaneous awareness of the emerging virus.

sources.author: Gertz, Bill
sources.title: Coronavirus link to China biowarfare program possible, analyst says

sources.author: Cohen, Jon
sources.title: Wuhan seafood market may not be source of novel virus spreading globally
sources.summary: Science news piece on the Lancet first-41-patients paper, noting the earliest case became ill on 1 December 2019 with no reported market link and arguing the Huanan seafood market may not be where the outbreak began.
sources.book_role: Brings market-origin doubts into Western scientific coverage at the same moment U.S. officials are absorbing the new virus.

sources.author: Norman, Joseph, et al.
sources.title: Systemic Risk of Pandemic via Novel Pathogens – Coronavirus: A Note
sources.summary: NECSI/NYU note by Norman, Bar-Yam, and Taleb arguing the new coronavirus poses systemic pandemic risk and that travel bans and precautionary responses should be taken seriously despite incomplete data.
sources.book_role: Early complex-systems warning that the outbreak should be treated as a fat-tailed pandemic threat, not a containable local event.

sources.title: Anthony Fauci’s Work Calendar
sources.summary: FOIA-released pages from Anthony Fauci’s official work calendar around the turn of 2019/2020, listing day-to-day NIAID meetings as the novel coronavirus emerges.
sources.book_role: Documentary schedule evidence for what Fauci was doing when emails and briefings about Wuhan-linked coronavirus work reach him.

sources.author: Folkers, Greg
sources.title: Email to Anthony Fauci on WIV, EcoHealth, NIAID Grant
sources.summary: FOIA email on draft talking points noting that NIAID-funded coronavirus experts—including Peter Daszak’s EcoHealth group with Ralph Baric and others—had been funded for coronavirus work in China via R01AI110964.
sources.book_role: The chapter’s central document: the message that puts EcoHealth, Baric, and NIAID China coronavirus funding directly into Fauci’s early briefings.

sources.author: Ting, Victor
sources.title: China coronavirus: Hong Kong medical experts call for ‘draconian’ measures in city as research estimates there are already 44,000 cases in Wuhan
sources.summary: SCMP report that HKU’s Gabriel Leung and colleagues urged ‘draconian’ Hong Kong measures after modelling suggested ~44,000 Wuhan infections and self-sustaining spread in major mainland cities.
sources.book_role: Shows how early academic modelling already implied far larger Wuhan caseloads than official counts—central to Chapter 4’s scale-of-outbreak argument.

sources.title: Novel Coronavirus (2019-nCoV) Situation Report – 7
sources.summary: WHO Situation Report 7 noting the Director-General’s Beijing mission, incubation-period estimates of about 2–10 days, and the need for better data on the infectious period including possible asymptomatic transmission.
sources.book_role: Official WHO snapshot of what was publicly known (and still uncertain) about spread and incubation in late January.

sources.author: Wuhan Institute of Virology
sources.title: Bat coronavirus RaTG13, complete genome

sources.book_role: The complete closest known relative sequence whose Mojiang provenance Chapter 11 reconstructs.

sources.author: Kuikanmäki, Jari, and Otto Juote
sources.title: Loppu on lähellä
sources.summary: YouTube episode of the Jari & Otto Show titled ‘Loppu on lähellä’ (28 Jan 2020). Video URLs are skipped under scrape policy; citation retained from the bibliography.
sources.book_role: Author’s own contemporaneous podcast reaction as the outbreak reaches Europe and Finland.

sources.title: Finland's first coronavirus case confirmed in Lapland
sources.summary: Yle report confirming Finland’s first coronavirus case: a Chinese tourist from Wuhan isolated in good condition at Lapland Central Hospital in Rovaniemi after travel via Saariselkä.
sources.book_role: Brings the outbreak into Finland—the author’s home frame for following early international spread.

sources.author: Baric, Ralph
sources.title: 2019-nHCoV
sources.publication: ODNI Biological Sciences Experts Group (BSEG) / U.S. Senate HSGAC

sources.title: Statement on the second meeting of the International Health Regulations (2005) Emergency Committee regarding the outbreak of novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV)
sources.summary: WHO statement from the second IHR Emergency Committee meeting on 2019-nCoV, the meeting that led to declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.
sources.book_role: Marks the formal international emergency declaration as cases begin appearing across Europe and beyond.

sources.author: Tan, Jianxing
sources.title: Li Wenliang, the “whistleblower” of the coronavirus outbreak: Truth matters more than rehabilitation
sources.summary: Caixin commentary/report (Wayback capture) on Li Wenliang as coronavirus whistleblower, arguing that establishing truth about early warnings matters more than symbolic rehabilitation.
sources.book_role: Contemporary Chinese investigative framing of Li Wenliang’s warning and the stakes of early information control.

sources.author: Sirotkin, Karl, and Dan Sirotkin
sources.title: Logistical and Technical Exploration into the Origins of the Wuhan Strain of Coronavirus (COVID-19)
sources.summary: Early January 2020 technical essay by Karl and Dan Sirotkin arguing logistical and genomic reasons to take a laboratory origin for the Wuhan coronavirus seriously.
sources.book_role: Example of very early independent technical skepticism about a natural-only origin while official narratives were still forming.

sources.title: Italy declares coronavirus emergency after first two cases confirmed
sources.summary: Reuters report that Italy declared a six-month state of emergency after two Chinese tourists from Wuhan tested positive, and halted flights to and from China.
sources.book_role: Documents Italy’s first confirmed cases and emergency powers; notes later cite even earlier undetected Italian spread.

sources.author: Rintala, Mirja
sources.title: The government was urged to respond to the spread of the coronavirus – now Minister Kiuru responds to MPs’ criticism
sources.summary: Iltasanomat piece in which Family and Care Services Minister Krista Kiuru answers MPs’ criticism of government quietness, saying Finland follows WHO and THL guidance and that virus control is not a political matter.
sources.book_role: Finnish political reaction as the first local case and European spread force the government on the defensive.

sources.author: Xiao, Botao, and Lei Xiao
sources.title: The possible origins of 2019-nCoV coronavirus (preprint)
sources.summary: Early February 2020 preprint discussing possible origins of 2019-nCoV, noting genomic similarity to bat CoV ZC45 and questioning whether the Huanan market alone explains the epidemic’s start.
sources.book_role: Early alternative-origin preprint circulating as the bat/pangolin narratives were being locked in.

sources.author: Shih, Gerry, et al.
sources.title: Early missteps and state secrecy in China probably allowed the coronavirus to spread farther and faster
sources.summary: Washington Post investigation of early Chinese official secrecy and missteps that likely let the virus spread farther and faster. Only a short opening was retrieved before the paywall.
sources.book_role: Documents Beijing’s early information control—the backdrop against which Western ‘conspiracy’ branding of origin questions takes shape.

sources.author: Fauci, Anthony
sources.title: Email to Hugh Auchincloss re: “Baric, Shi et al – Nature Medicine – SARS Gain of Function”
sources.summary: DocumentCloud landing for the Leopold NIH FOIA dump of Anthony Fauci emails (3,234 pages), including the 1 Feb 2020 note to Hugh Auchincloss on the Baric–Shi Nature Medicine SARS gain-of-function paper. Viewer chrome retrieved; full email text not extracted.
sources.book_role: FOIA backbone for the Feb 1 conference-call / Proximal Origin inception story Chapter 10 revisits as floodgates open.

sources.author: Zhou, Peng, et al.
sources.title: A pneumonia outbreak associated with a new coronavirus of probable bat origin
sources.summary: Nature paper from Shi Zhengli’s group identifying 2019-nCoV as a new SARS-related coronavirus of probable bat origin, reporting characterization of the Wuhan outbreak virus and its relationship to bat SARSr-CoVs (later tied to the RaTG13 narrative).
sources.book_role: Foundational WIV Nature paper asserting probable bat origin—the scientific frame Chapter 5 interrogates alongside pangolin and market claims.

sources.author: Choi, David
sources.title: Republican senator suggests 'worse than Chernobyl' coronavirus could've come from Chinese 'superlaboratory'
sources.summary: Business Insider coverage of Sen. Tom Cotton suggesting at a Senate hearing that the coronavirus—‘worse than Chernobyl’—might have come from a Chinese ‘superlaboratory’ and that Beijing had misled about the outbreak.
sources.book_role: Early high-profile U.S. political airing of a Wuhan-lab hypothesis that media soon labeled fringe/conspiracy.

sources.author: BBC News
sources.title: Li Wenliang: Coronavirus kills Chinese whistleblower doctor
sources.summary: BBC report on the death of Li Wenliang from COVID-19, recounting his early WeChat warning, police admonishment, infection while working at Wuhan Central Hospital, and the public anger that followed.
sources.book_role: Closes the Prologue’s whistleblower thread with the internationally reported death of Li Wenliang.

sources.author: Cyranoski, David
sources.title: Did pangolins spread the China coronavirus to people?
sources.summary: Nature news report on Guangzhou researchers suggesting pangolins as the probable intermediate animal source of the coronavirus outbreak then infecting tens of thousands.
sources.book_role: Introduces the pangolin-intermediate-host hypothesis that gives the chapter its title and competing origin narrative.

sources.author: Kuo, Lily
sources.title: Coronavirus: journalist missing in Wuhan as anger towards Chinese authorities grows
sources.summary: Guardian report on citizen journalist Chen Qiushi going missing in Wuhan amid anger after Li Wenliang’s death, with claims authorities were silencing another whistleblower.
sources.book_role: Shows continued suppression of independent reporting from Wuhan while origin questions were being policed abroad as ‘rumors.’

sources.title: Anthony Fauci’s Work Calendar, Meeting with Dr Ralph Baric
sources.summary: OpenTheBooks release of Fauci’s Nov 2019–Mar 2020 calendar, including early NSC/White House coronavirus meetings and the February 2020 Baric meeting entry.
sources.book_role: Pins the Fauci–Baric meeting on the official calendar that structures Chapter 3’s chronology.

sources.author: Beilfuss, Lisa
sources.title: China’s Coronavirus Figures Don’t Add Up. ‘This Never Happens With Real Data.’
sources.summary: Barron’s piece arguing China’s coronavirus statistics look too perfect to be trustworthy, echoing long-standing skepticism about Chinese official data. Full article behind subscription; only lede retrieved.
sources.book_role: Supports the chapter’s skepticism about official Chinese case numbers while origin stories (bats vs pangolins) were being sold.

sources.title: Russian Disinformation Apparatus Taking Advantage of Coronavirus Concerns
sources.summary: U.S. Global Engagement Center report tracking Russia-linked personas amplifying coronavirus themes in multiple languages from late January 2020 as part of a broader disinformation apparatus.
sources.book_role: Primary U.S. government document used to frame early origin/lab talk as foreign disinformation rather than open scientific debate.

sources.author: Ibbetson, Ross
sources.title: Did coronavirus originate in Chinese government laboratory?
sources.summary: Daily Mail report on the Xiao/Xiao preprint arguing the virus likely came from a Wuhan lab (WHCDC and/or WIV), citing bat research near the Huanan market, bat–researcher accidents, and the distance of native bats from Wuhan.
sources.book_role: Brings the lab-origin reading of the Xiao preprint into mass media while pangolin and bat-market stories were still the official line.

sources.author: Stevenson, Alexandra
sources.title: Senator Tom Cotton Repeats Fringe Theory of Coronavirus Origins
sources.summary: New York Times piece framing Cotton’s Wuhan-lab comments as a fringe origin theory. Firecrawl cannot scrape nytimes.com on this plan; citation retained.
sources.book_role: Exhibit of prestige-media ‘fringe theory’ branding that Chapter 6 argues shut down legitimate origin questions.

sources.author: Firozi, Paulina
sources.title: Tom Cotton repeats debunked conspiracy theory about coronavirus
sources.summary: Washington Post politics piece that originally called Cotton’s Wuhan-research comments a debunked conspiracy theory; a later correction removed ‘debunked’/‘conspiracy theory’ language. Only partial text retrieved.
sources.book_role: Key example of media ‘conspiracy theory’ labeling—and a later correction that Chapter 6 uses to show how overconfident that labeling was.

sources.author: Kuikanmäki, Jari, and Otto Juote
sources.title: Everything is Under Control

sources.author: Frieman, Matt

sources.summary: FOIA Slack notification in which Matt Frieman says Ralph Baric sat in Fauci’s office talking about the outbreak and chimeras, bristled at a WIV-link joke, and claimed Shi’s paper lacked Chinese government approval.
sources.book_role: Contemporaneous lab-world message corroborating a Fauci–Baric ‘outbreak and chimeras’ conversation in February 2020.

sources.author: Dong, Ensheng, Du, Hongru, and Gardner, Lauren
sources.title: An interactive web-based dashboard to track COVID-19 in real time
sources.summary: Lancet Infectious Diseases note introducing the Johns Hopkins interactive COVID-19 dashboard. Full text was not retrieved (paywall/chrome only).

sources.author: Calisher, Charles, et al.

sources.summary: Lancet multi-author statement supporting Chinese scientists and condemning conspiracy theories that COVID-19 lacked a natural origin. Full text not retrieved (paywall/chrome).

sources.author: Cohen, Jon
sources.title: Scientists ‘strongly condemn' rumors and conspiracy theories about origin of coronavirus outbreak
sources.summary: Science news coverage of the 27-scientist Lancet statement condemning rumors that COVID-19 came from a Wuhan lab and warning that such talk threatened open data sharing.
sources.book_role: Shows how quickly elite scientific media echoed and legitimized the Lancet condemnation of lab-origin hypotheses.

sources.author: Racaniello, Vincent
sources.title: Pangolins and the origin of SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus
sources.summary: Racaniello blog discussing pangolin CoVs, RaTG13 RBD differences, and the SARS-CoV-2 furin cleavage site absent from RaTG13—early technical framing of origin clues.
sources.book_role: Early technical discussion of spike features that later Mojiang/RaTG13 arguments build on.

sources.title: Russia-linked disinformation campaign fueling coronavirus alarm, US says

sources.author: Chung, Jane, and Emily Chow
sources.title: Concern over coronavirus spread as cases jump in South Korea, Italy and Iran

sources.book_role: Documents the late-February multi-country jump that undercuts ‘everything under control’ messaging.

sources.summary: Yle report quoting THL’s Mika Salminen calling Italy’s municipal lockdowns excessive and saying Italians were caught badly off guard—as Europe’s first major outbreak unfolds in northern Italy.
sources.book_role: Finnish official voice insisting Italy overreacted—local color for the ‘everything under control’ complacency theme.

sources.author: Liu, Shan-Lu, et al.
sources.title: No credible evidence supporting claims of the laboratory engineering of SARS-CoV-2
sources.summary: Liu, Saif, Weiss & Su commentary asserting no credible evidence of laboratory engineering of SARS-CoV-2—early published dismissal of lab-origin claims.
sources.book_role: Public scientific denial piece Chapter 11 contrasts with the authors’ private email doubts (s18).

sources.author: Baric, Ralph
sources.title: Presentation to the Congressional Biomedical Research Caucus
sources.summary: Congressional Biomedical Research Caucus presentation video. YouTube skipped.
sources.book_role: Video testimony/presentation in the biomedical caucus series.

sources.title: Novel Coronavirus (COVID‑19) Situation Report 39
sources.summary: WHO Situation Report 39 raising global spread/impact risk to ‘very high,’ noting new countries reporting cases, the WHO–China Joint Mission findings, and—as the book notes—continued advice against travel/trade restrictions.
sources.book_role: Official WHO snapshot combining rising risk assessment with advice against travel restrictions—the control narrative Chapter 7 critiques.

sources.author: Zhuang, Pinghui

sources.book_role: Shows early Chinese authorities punishing the lab that shared the genome—aftermath of information control, not openness.

sources.author: Gao, Yu, et al.
sources.title: How early signs of the coronavirus were spotted, spread and throttled in China
sources.summary: Straits Times / Caixin investigation: Chinese labs sequenced a SARS-like virus by late December—days before WHO notification and weeks before public confirmation of human-to-human spread—while alerts failed to trigger a public response.
sources.book_role: Reconstructs how early genomic warnings were throttled inside China’s system—core to the aftermath blame and cover-up debate.

sources.title: Coronavirus: Italy extends emergency measures nationwide
sources.summary: BBC report that Italy extended coronavirus emergency measures nationwide, with Conte ordering people to stay home as deaths jumped and cases rose across all regions—then the worst-hit country after China.
sources.book_role: Shows Europe’s first full national lockdown as the ‘under control’ narrative collapses.

sources.author: Andersen, Kristian, et al.

sources.book_role: The chapter’s central scientific document: ‘Proximal Origin,’ used to condemn lab-leak ideas as scientifically closed.

sources.author: Defense Intelligence Agency

sources.summary: DIA authoritative assessment document on SARS-CoV-2 origins.
sources.book_role: Primary DIA origins assessment text among Chapter 19’s declassifications.

sources.author: Myers, Steven, and Chris Buckley
sources.title: China Created a Fail-Safe System to Track Contagions. It Failed.
sources.summary: New York Times investigation of how China’s post-SARS contagion-alert system failed in the early COVID outbreak. NYT is blocked by Firecrawl as an unsupported site.
sources.book_role: Documents the collapse of China’s supposed early-warning system—central to the outbreak’s preventable aftermath.

sources.author: Coutard, B, et al.

sources.book_role: Scientific marker of the unusual furin cleavage site—key technical anomaly while public messaging still claimed control.

sources.author: Cadell, Cate, and Yawen Chen

sources.book_role: Documents the information-control environment surrounding any Wuhan/Mojiang origins inquiry.

sources.author: Birrell, Ian
sources.title: How China muzzled its Bat Woman: Beijing authorities hushed up the findings of a scientist who unlocked the genetic make-up of the coronavirus
sources.summary: Investigative article arguing Chinese authorities constrained public discussion of early genomic findings and origin questions around Shi Zhengli and related research. Used in the book’s notes as evidence of suppression during early reporting.
sources.book_role: Supports the Prologue notes’ claim that Shi’s early interviews occurred amid active suppression of origin discussion.

sources.author: Rogin, Josh
sources.title: State Department cables warned of safety issues at Wuhan lab studying bat coronaviruses
sources.summary: Josh Rogin opinion based on 2018 U.S. Embassy cables warning of safety and staffing weaknesses at WIV’s BSL-4 bat-coronavirus research—and the risk of a SARS-like pandemic—years before COVID.
sources.book_role: Brings pre-pandemic U.S. diplomatic warnings about WIV biosafety into the aftermath origins fight (cables later declassified per chapter notes).

sources.author: Rosen, Guy
sources.title: An Update on Our Work to Keep People Informed and Limit Misinformation About COVID-19
sources.summary: Facebook/Meta integrity update expanding removal of COVID false claims; the page also records the later policy shift that they would no longer remove ‘COVID-19 is man-made’ claims amid origins investigations.
sources.book_role: Platform enforcement backdrop: lab-origin talk treated as removable misinformation while WHO/China narratives dominated.

sources.title: Remarks by President Trump, Vice President Pence, and Members of the Coronavirus Task Force in Press Briefing
sources.summary: Archived April 17, 2020 task-force briefing transcript; includes press questions tying a Wuhan BSL-4 lab to NIH funding of Chinese research—early public collision of lab-origin and U.S. grant politics later reopened in 2021.
sources.book_role: Shows the lab/funding question was already live in 2020 briefings—before being shouted down, then revived when floodgates opened.

sources.author: Daszak, Peter

sources.summary: Daszak tweet framing trust as Fauci versus ‘politicized conspiracy theorists.’ No URL in source data; citation retained from bibliography.
sources.book_role: Voice of the WHO-team scientist policing origins doubt as conspiracy while conflicts of interest went undeclared.

sources.author: Deigin, Yuri
sources.title: Lab-Made? SARS-CoV-2 Genealogy Through the Lens of Gain-of-Function Research

sources.book_role: Influential early GoF-genealogy argument that Chapter 3 pairs with the Fauci/Baric/WIV funding thread.

sources.author: Morens, David
sources.title: Email to Peter Daszak
